also: what do you do for a living?

terms.gloss: a living, paid work, a way of earning
evidence: Plaut. Rud. 2.1.2: pauperēs hominēs, quibus nec quaestus est (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally gain, profit: the work one lives by, seen as what it earns. It can be any trade, decent or not (quaestuī habēre, to make money out of something), so it is not a word of praise. For the trade as a skill, see trade (artificium); for a single piece of work or a job to be done, see job (opus).
Work as a task, not as a livelihood: opus nōn habet, he has nothing to do. See job.

evidence: Traupman 341, 353: quaestum facere; quem quaestum facis?, what is your occupation?
terms.comment: Take care: in Plautus and Terence quaestum facere on its own is said of a prostitute (Lewis & Short s.v. quaestus); vīctum quaeritāre, which Traupman also gives, is safer.

phrases.latin: pauperēs hominēs, quibus nec quaestus est
phrases.english: poor men, who have no living

sources: Lewis & Short: quaestus · Lewis & Short: opus
